An engine-driven unit stays outdoors with exhaust kept away from doors, windows and air intakes. Hoses reach the collection point without moving the engine into an enclosed work area. The operator follows the chosen pump’s suction and discharge limits.

sections.title: Charge the casing before trying to lift water
paragraphs: With the unit stopped, the operator fills the pump casing through its designated priming opening and closes it as directed. The initial water allows the pump to purge air from its suction path. Running a dry centrifugal casing longer is not a substitute for this preparation and can damage the equipment.

If a stopped setup drains back through the suction hose, restarting may require priming again. Where the pump instructions support it, a suitable suction foot valve can retain that water column. sections.title: Confirm delivery before continuing the recovery

Loading direction, rug size and machine limits govern the setup. Severe shaking calls for stopping and correcting the load after the drum comes fully to rest. sections.title: Finish drying before the rug returns

sections.title: Transfer the weak area’s load to a compatible backing
paragraphs: The conservator selects and prepares suitable support fabric and thread, with colorfastness and weight considered. Work is carried out on a flat support. Overly strong thread or tight stitching can cut or gather the original fibers instead of stabilizing them.

Where appropriate, laid stitches span a weak area and extend into stronger surrounding fabric. Smaller crossing stitches secure them to the backing, distributing support without pulling the damage closed. Existing openings are used where possible, and stitch tension remains relaxed. This joins the textile to a lasting support rather than relying on a temporary screen during vacuuming.

sections.title: Match handling and display to the repaired condition
